meta.plant_name: Lea County Data Center power station

Status.note:
Re-verified, no change.

Status:
- The Business Wire release from November 6, 2025 at https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251106765936/en/New-Era-Energy-Digital-Enters-into-Land-Option-Purchase-Agreement-for-3500-Acres-in-New-Mexico-for-7GW-AI-Data-Center-Hub-Marks-first-Wholly-Owned-Development-Separate-from-TCDC-Joint-Venture says New Era entered a land option for about 3,500 acres in Lea County and 'more than 2 gigawatts (GW) of natural gas generation'. It says engineering would begin within 30 days.
- An Albuquerque Journal article at https://www.abqjournal.com/business/texas-company-eyes-lea-county-for-data-center-campus/2902150 repeats this.
- The company's locations page at https://www.newerainfra.ai/locations (published September 2026) lists Lea County as 'Next Phase', 7+ GW, a 10 to 15 year phased buildout. No permit, tenant or construction is reported. So the unit stays announced.

units.notes: No update found beyond the November 2025 announcement and the company's September 2026 locations page. No air permit, queue entry, county record or SEC filing naming a turbine design or engine count was found in the harvest. Technology stays unknown and Backup Power has no document that states it.

qa.question: Should Turbine/Engine Technology stay unknown for the Lea County Data Center?
qa.finding: No source names a design. The Business Wire release only says more than 2 GW of natural gas generation with confirmed gas supply.
qa.recommendation: Leave the technology as unknown and recheck when an air permit application or county record names the equipment.

The SPP queue entry GEN-2006-026 in the brief is a 604 MW operating Hobbs-area gas entry from 2006 and does not belong to this project.
